subject.title: [Feature Request] Code Verification and Signature for Skills

question: What trust model should OpenClaw enforce for SKILL.md skills before prompt loading and capability use?
rationale: This choice sets the security boundary for publisher or registry trust roots, revocation, unsigned compatibility, persisted metadata, ClawHub policy, and capability enforcement; automation cannot safely choose those semantics from source inspection alone.

options.title: Design canonical signed-skill model
options.body: Define signatures, trust roots, persisted expected content, runtime reverify, revocation, status surfaces, and unsigned migration policy before implementation.

options.title: Keep verification advisory for now
options.body: Treat current ClawHub verification and local hashes as operator information only until a broader security profile lands.

options.title: Land narrow hash checks separately
options.body: Allow installed-file drift checks such as the open ClawHub verification PR to land as groundwork without treating this issue as complete.

recommendation.title: Design canonical signed-skill model
recommendation.body: Define signatures, trust roots, persisted expected content, runtime reverify, revocation, status surfaces, and unsigned migration policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest visible owner for native ClawHub skill install behavior and prior security-product review of this issue.
